recommended_approach: Mantaflow Liquid Domain (FLIP-style liquid) + continuous Flow Inflow (Use Plane Init) + Effector Collision (glass/table) + Liquid Mesh generation (Cycles render)

key_parameters.bake_note: Apply object scale before baking (seen in technique using bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)).

warnings: Doc search returned limited direct Blender Python API attribute documentation for Mantaflow (tool warning: “No API doc_refs found (expected bpy.types.* or bpy.ops.* references).”).
Ensure the Domain fully contains: inflow stream path, entire glass bowl, and all splash trajectories; otherwise liquid/mesh will clip at domain bounds (Domain concept noted in Fluid Introduction).
Apply scale on Domain/Flow/Effector objects before baking to avoid mismatched voxel sizing and collision thickness issues (technique example uses bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)).
Thin glass meshes can cause collision leaks; use sufficient thickness (e.g., Solidify) and/or an additional hidden collision ‘disc’ at the base/stem junction (pattern: glass_bottom_collision_disc).
Inflow from a non-planar emitter can wobble/break up; the Flow setting ‘Use Plane Init’ is documented under Flow settings and is commonly used for stable inflows.
alternative_approaches: Mantaflow Liquid + secondary droplets via a separate particle/instancing system (art-direct escaping rim droplets while keeping the main pour/volume physically simulated).
Mantaflow Liquid + additional ‘secondary’ simulation layer (e.g., spray/foam-style detail) to enhance splashes without raising the main domain resolution.
